priorBlockerClosure.evidenceOrGap: declareDiscoveryExtension now invoked with the SDK-correct shape: top-level method/bodyType + raw `input` body + separate `inputSchema` + `output: { example, schema }`. Verified against installed @x402/extensions/bazaar createBodyDiscoveryExtension at node_modules/@x402/extensions/dist/cjs/bazaar/index.js:153-230 — `body: input` (line 168) sets info.input.body to the RAW example; `body: inputSchema` (line 197) puts the schema under schema.properties.input.properties.body. Decorative top-level fields removed (no longer present on extensions object outside the {bazaar:...} wrapper). PROP-005 tier-0 tests at __tests__/server-self-facilitate.test.js:150-185 assert the SDK-aligned shape directly.

Replaced unreachable Express error handler with wrapSettle(settleFn) at L78-89: catches any throw from the wrapped settle, logs `[x402.settle.error] <code> <msg>` to stderr, then re-raises the original error so @x402/express performs the SDK-defined response. Wired at L255 by passing `settle: wrapSettle(facilitator.settle.bind(facilitator))` to x402ResourceServer. Verified the wrap is actually reached: paymentMiddleware → x402HTTPResourceServer.processSettlement (core/server line 2289) → calls back through facilitatorClient.settle (core/server line 1452 / 1464) which IS our wrapped function. The contract `[x402.settle.error] LOG + RETHROW` is the impl invariant; spec amendment validation note below clarifies a remaining spec-vs-SDK gap on the SDK's response BODY shape.

CORS now uses `allowedHeaders: ['Content-Type','Authorization','X-PAYMENT']` and `exposedHeaders: ['X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE']`. The non-existent 'X-Payment-*' wildcard syntax from iter-1 is gone. Browser preflight will now match the x402 spec's singular `X-PAYMENT` request header and surface `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE` on the response.

Replaced basename `process.argv[1].endsWith('server.js')` with the canonical ESM entrypoint check: `__isEntry = typeof process.argv[1] === 'string' && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href`. `pathToFileURL` import added at L9. This is exactly iter-1's fix option (a) verbatim. Standard `node src/server.js` (absolute or relative cwd) → both URLs resolve identically and match. `node -e "import('./src/server.js')"` → argv[1]='[eval]' → pathToFileURL('[eval]')='file:///cwd/%5Beval%5D' which does NOT match import.meta.url, so the listener is correctly disabled (no silent boot of a partial server). The pm2/dumb-init launcher edge case is acknowledged but not the canonical Node entrypoint shape, so the fix is complete per iter-1's proposal.

createApp() now performs the REQ-004b runtime assertion: `const resolved = resolveAcceptsAmount(ROUTES['POST /social/x'].accepts); if (resolved !== '3000') throw new Error('REQ-004b violation: ...')`. This fires BEFORE the in-process facilitator wiring and BEFORE app.listen(), so a Tier-2 replicator who edits PRICE_LITERAL silently to '$0.30' (or flips USDC to an 18-decimal asset) sees the boot fail loudly. Cheap, defense-in-depth — matches the iter-1 suggested fix verbatim.

REQ-014-SDK-alignment.evidence: Spec REQ-014 (behavioral-spec.md:48) claims: 'the installed @x402/express paymentMiddleware performs the SDK-defined response (HTTP 402 with body { "error": "Settlement failed", "details": <message> }, per @x402/express/dist/cjs/index.js lines 256-273 + 281-291)'. Installed @x402/express is 2.17.0 (node_modules/@x402/express/package.json:3), NOT the 2.4.0 the spec references. The actual installed SDK code at node_modules/@x402/express/dist/cjs/index.js:344-353 reads: `} catch (error) { if (error instanceof FacilitatorResponseError) { ... sendFacilitatorError(res, error); return; } console.error(error); bufferedCalls = []; res.status(402).json({}); return; }` — i.e. an UNEXPECTED settle exception (the wrapSettle rethrow path) produces `res.status(402).json({})` with an EMPTY body, NOT `{ error: 'Settlement failed', details: <message> }`. The FacilitatorResponseError path (line 141-143) is `res.status(502).json({ error: error.message })` — 502, not 402, and `{ error }` only. The cited spec line ranges 256-273 and 281-291 in the installed file are inside the writeHead/write/end buffering shim and the handler-invoke try/catch, NOT the 402 response. Therefore: the impl's `log + rethrow` contract is correctly implemented and the impl satisfies REQ-014 LITERALLY; but the SPEC's characterization of what the SDK responds with is stale (anchored to a version-and-line-number that no longer exists in the installed package). A Tier-2 replicator reading the spec will expect a `{error,details}` settle-failure body and get an empty `{}` — buyer-facing contract drift. (NOT a blocker for impl PASS — the impl matches the spec's contract — but logged here as an outstanding spec maintenance item.)

REQ-005-SDK-alignment.evidence: Spec REQ-005 (behavioral-spec.md:30) claims the SDK returns `{ bazaar: { info: { input: { type:"http", method, bodyType, body: <input> }, output: { type:"json", example } }, schema: {...} } }`. Verified against node_modules/@x402/extensions/dist/cjs/bazaar/index.js:153-230 (createBodyDiscoveryExtension) and L317-326 (declareDiscoveryExtension wraps the return as `{ bazaar: extension }` when not MCP-shaped). Specifically: L168 sets `body: input` (raw example flows through); L171-176 emits `output: { type: 'json', example: output.example }` when output.example is truthy; L197 sets `body: inputSchema` in the JSON schema sub-tree at schema.properties.input.properties.body — exactly the assertion in PROP-005 tier-0 test #3 at __tests__/server-self-facilitate.test.js:174-184. The impl's SOCIAL_X_INPUT_SCHEMA has type:'object' and properties:{query,kind,limit} — non-empty — so `Object.keys(bodySchema.properties).length > 0` is robust. REQ-005 amendment aligns exactly with installed SDK.

findings.issue: SPEC-side (not impl-side) drift: REQ-014 anchors its SDK-behavior claim to @x402/express 2.4.0 and to specific line numbers (256-273 + 281-291) that do not exist in the installed 2.17.0 file. Installed SDK responds with `res.status(402).json({})` (empty body) on the wrapSettle rethrow path — not `{ error: 'Settlement failed', details }`. Impl SATISFIES the spec contract (`[x402.settle.error]` log + rethrow), so this is NOT an impl finding; it is a spec maintenance item. Logged here for visibility — does not block this iter-2 verdict because the spec's normative contract on the IMPL is met.
findings.fix: (Spec maintenance, not impl) Amend behavioral-spec.md REQ-014 to drop the specific 2.4.0 line-number citation and either (a) state the SDK responds with whatever it responds with — impl contract is log+rethrow only — or (b) re-verify against installed 2.17.0 and document the actual `res.status(402).json({})` empty-body behavior so Tier-2 replicators don't anchor on a fictional `{error,details}` shape.

findings.issue: PARTIAL closure of iter-1 edge_cases-1. The silent-catch is gone — the catch now logs `[x402.boot.gas_probe_error] address=<addr> reason=<msg>` (L199-203). However the fire-and-forget shape remains: `gasReady` starts at `false` (L187) and is only flipped after the promise resolves. A `/health` hit that lands within the RPC round-trip after boot returns `gas_ready:false` even for a funded wallet. iter-1 finding was NOT in the 8 blockers list so deferral is acceptable; raising as PASS-with-observation. Optional follow-up: tri-state `'true'|'false'|'unknown'` so the heartbeat can distinguish 'probed and broke' from 'never successfully probed'.
findings.fix: Optional (not blocking): change `let gasReady = false` to `let gasReady = 'unknown'`, set to `'true'`/`'false'` on probe resolve/reject, and serialize in the `/health` body. Or simply await the probe before app.listen() (NFR-003 budget is 2s, probe RTT is ~200ms on Base mainnet, fits the budget).

findings.issue: Minor flake risk. The PROP-011 test waits a hard 2000ms before tearing down the child (line 291: `setTimeout(() => res(), 2000)`). With the X402_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1 override, the server prints `listening on port` in ~50-100ms — but the test always blocks 2s. On a slow CI runner the test could brush against the vitest default timeout. Not a regression vs iter-1 (iter-1 also took ~2s) and the test PASSES in iter-2 GREEN (2002ms reported). Optional polish: stream stdout, resolve as soon as `/listening on port/` matches, kill the child immediately — drops the test to <500ms and removes the implicit timeout coupling.
findings.fix: (Optional, non-blocking) Replace the fixed-2s timer with an event-driven match: `child.stdout.on('data', d => { stdout += d; if (/listening on port/.test(stdout)) { resolved = true; res(); } })` and only fall back to the 2s timer if the line never appears.
